gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Noto Sans Sundanese lays its curves out with plenty of daylight, and the lowercase stands tall. Styro is the opposite, a retro display face with crowded letters, best at making a loud entrance, while the plain sans body is best at staying open and readable.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Retro swagger meets open curves. Styro packs its big lowercase tight and commanding, while Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in every bend, with short ascender stems keeping the sans body friendly.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Styro crowds its big lowercase into a retro, commanding shout, with e and c barely letting any light through. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri then lets a long run of text breathe, its tall x-height and open-bowled a keeping the sans-serif lines easy to follow.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eastern: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern reads in a friendly, contemporary way, its tall lowercase standing against small caps and curve endings that keep their distance. Styro's tight retro letters would feel dense over a long passage, but the sans-serif body keeps going without any strain.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-syriac-western: Styro's letters are pressed so close they nearly touch, a retro, commanding crush of big lowercase. Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far back from the stroke, so a longer stretch reads like tidy bundles of small, tall letters.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Noto Sans Tagalog fills the middle of each line with generous curves, giving the text a lightly open, modern texture. Styro supplies the retro, commanding punch with crowded letters, and the sans-serif body gives the eye somewhere roomy to rest below it.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Crowded retro punch, then open air. Noto Sans Tagbanwa keeps its curves clearly gapped and its lowercase filling most of the height, so the sans body gives Styro's tight, commanding letters some welcome breathing space.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its strokes off before they touch, so the text feels soft and approachable, with barely any step up to the capitals. Over many lines it stays gentle.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Noto Sans Tai Tham reads like chalkboard lowercase pushing up toward the capital line, with every c clearly open to the eye. Its openness against Styro's crowded, retro, commanding letters is what makes the pair stand out.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Styro's big lowercase is pressed tight, with e and c barely open, giving it a retro, commanding look. Noto Sans Tai Viet answers on the page with short ascenders, a tall x-height and terminals pulled back from each curve.
